observation.visible_scene: A close-up view of a person in a green sleeve and dark vest using a cordless drill on a light-colored wooden frame structure, likely a bench or table under assembly. The frame includes straight rails, a curved top rail, and several pre-drilled holes or fastener points. The drill is the main moving object, held by one or two hands and positioned against different parts of the wooden frame.
visible_changes: At the start, the drill is held roughly horizontal with its bit near a hole or fastener location on the right-side rail; the bit remains in approximately the same area through the first several frames while the grip and drill angle shift slightly.
Around 1.2–1.6 seconds, the drill is lifted and moved away from the right-side rail; the bit becomes visible separated from the wood and points toward the upper/right side of the frame.
From about 1.6–2.4 seconds, the drill is repositioned leftward and rotated into a more vertical orientation, with the person’s hands adjusting around the tool body.
From roughly 2.4 seconds to the end, the drill bit is brought into contact with a hole or fastener location on the left-side rail, where it remains held vertically with small positional adjustments.

The wooden frame itself stays largely in place throughout the excerpt, while the drill and the person’s hands move across it; any change in framing appears small and may be due to slight camera or body movement rather than object motion of the frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the drill is actively driving a screw, drilling a hole, or merely positioning the bit cannot be confirmed from the still samples alone.
What happens before the segment begins and after it ends is not visible.
Whether the fastener or hole on the right side was completed before the tool moved away is unknown.
The exact function or final state of the wooden structure is not shown.
uncertain_details: The precise amount of camera movement is uncertain because the background and frame edges change only slightly.
The drill’s rotation or operating state is not directly visible in still frames.
The material identity of the wood and the exact nature of the fasteners are inferred only from appearance.
Some motion blur in the middle frames makes the exact path of the drill’s repositioning less certain.
